# Culture & Society

Topics on the culture, media, social life, and everyday society of South Korea, from traditional heritage to its contemporary global cultural exports.

<!-- BEGIN GENERATED: category-index — maintained by build-structure; do not edit by hand -->
- [Hallyu (Korean Wave)](hallyu.md) — The global rise of South Korean popular culture — K-pop, K-drama, film, and beauty — and its emergence as a soft-power phenomenon.
- [Korean Cuisine and Food Culture](korean-cuisine.md) — The fermentation-centered food tradition of South Korea, from kimchi and the kimjang custom to its global spread through the Korean Wave.
- [Religion and Buddhism in Korea](religion-and-buddhism.md) — Korea's layered religious history — shamanism, Buddhism, Confucianism, and the explosive 20th-century growth of Christianity — and its contemporary multi-religious, increasingly secular society.
- [Education and Universities in South Korea](education-and-universities.md) — The intense, test-driven education system, the "SKY" university hierarchy, the hagwon economy, and the demographic and equity pressures reshaping it.
- [K-pop Industry and Global Music Market](kpop-industry.md) — The trainee-driven entertainment industry, its major companies, and its rise from a domestic sector to a globally dominant cultural and economic force.
- [Sports and the Olympic Games](sports-and-olympics.md) — South Korea's rise as an Olympic, football, golf, and esports power, and the use of athletic success as national soft power alongside the Korean Wave.
- [Film and Cinema Industry](film-cinema-industry.md) — The Korean film industry from colonial-era "Arirang" to Bong Joon-ho's "Parasite" and the streaming era, and its emergence as a global cultural export.
- [Architecture and Urban Design in South Korea](architecture-urban-design.md) — Korean architecture and city-building from the hanok tradition through developmental-state apartment complexes to contemporary landmarks and smart cities.
- [Hangul and the Korean Alphabet](hangul.md) — The featural alphabet created under King Sejong in the 1440s, its scientific design and syllable-block structure, its colonial-era preservation, and its role as a symbol of Korean identity and literacy.
- [Webtoons and Digital Comics](webtoons.md) — The mobile-first, vertical-scroll digital comics format pioneered by Naver and Kakao; a platform-driven creative industry and a fast-growing "third pillar" of Hallyu feeding drama, film, and anime adaptations worldwide.
- [Gaming Industry in South Korea](gaming-industry.md) — The multi-billion-dollar game industry — Nexon, NCSoft, Krafton, and Smilegate — from PC-bang and *StarCraft* origins to global MMORPG, mobile, and battle-royale leadership, its esports culture, and its regulatory debates.
- [Korean Literature and Literary Culture](korean-literature.md) — Two millennia of Korean poetry, fiction, and scholarship — from *hyangga* and *sijo* through pansori and colonial-era poets to Han Kang's 2024 Nobel Prize in Literature.
- [Korean Drama Industry](korean-drama-industry.md) — The serialized-television sector of the Korean Wave, from *Winter Sonata* and *Dae Jang Geum* to Netflix-era global hits like *Crash Landing on You* and *Squid Game*.
- [Korean Traditional Visual Arts](traditional-visual-arts.md) — Two millennia of painting, calligraphy, Buddhist sculpture, and ceramics — from Goryeo celadon and the Joseon moon jar to the modern Dansaekhwa monochrome movement.
- [Korean Broadcast Television Industry](korean-broadcast-television.md) — The KBS/MBC/SBS terrestrial network system — its state/commercial hybrid structure, the evening-drama and music-show production model, its regulatory and political flashpoints, and its role in mass media and soft power distinct from the film and streaming ecosystems.
- [Seoul National University](seoul-national-university.md) — The nation's flagship university and apex of the "SKY" hierarchy — its 1946 founding, the Gwanak campus and activist legacy, its research standing, and its role as a symbol of meritocratic aspiration and educational inequality.
- [Chuseok — Korea's Harvest Festival](chuseok.md) — The mid-autumn harvest holiday and quintessential family celebration; ancestral rites, songpyeon and feasting, the mass return migration to hometowns, and its modern social and commercial dimensions.
- [Korean Royal Palaces and Heritage Sites](korean-royal-palaces.md) — The five grand Joseon palaces of Seoul — Gyeongbokgung, Changdeokgung, Changgyeonggung, Deoksugung, and Gyeonghuigung — and Suwon's Hwaseong Fortress; their architecture and geomancy, colonial-era destruction, ongoing restoration, and role as living heritage.
- [Seollal — Korea's Lunar New Year](seollal.md) — Korea's most significant traditional holiday; the *charye* ancestral rite, tteokguk and *sebae*, the Great Migration to ancestral hometowns, and its gender, generational, diaspora, and commercial dimensions.
- [Women's Movements and Gender Equality in South Korea](womens-movements-and-gender-equality.md) — The arc of Korean women's activism from anti-colonial and labor struggles through 1990s institutional feminism to the digital-era mobilizations of the 2010s–2020s (#MeToo, the molka and Hyehwa protests, escape-the-corset, and 4B), set against a persistent gender pay gap, the world's lowest birth rate, and a fierce generational backlash.
- [Korean Language and Linguistics](korean-language.md) — The Korean language and its structure — agglutinative grammar, the honorific and speech-level system, Sino-Korean and English loanword strata, regional dialects, language policy and the Sejong Institutes, digital-era change, and North–South divergence.
- [Korean Fashion and Clothing Industry](korean-fashion.md) — Korean dress and fashion from the traditional hanbok to the contemporary K-fashion sector — Dongdaemun and the DDP, designers on the Paris runways, streetwear and the K-pop "idol effect," and fashion's place in Hallyu soft power.
- [Taekwondo and Korean Martial Arts](taekwondo-martial-arts.md) — Taekwondo — the Olympic Korean martial art — and the wider ecosystem of hapkido, tang soo do, the UNESCO-listed taekkyeon and ssireum, and gumdo, spanning technique, philosophy, competition, and soft power.
- [Confucianism and Neo-Confucianism in Korea](confucianism-and-neo-confucianism.md) — The philosophy that shaped Korean statecraft, family, and education from the Three Kingdoms through Joseon to the present; Neo-Confucian orthodoxy and the Four-Seven Debate, yangban society and the seowon academies, the Sirhak reform school, gender hierarchy, and the enduring legacy in modern education and social values.
